feedback: If a learner predicts the inflated and deflated ball weigh the same 'because air weighs nothing', surface this as the target misconception and have them compare the balance readings — air has mass

If a learner says pressure only pushes down, use the card-on-upturned-glass result to show air pushing upward (and, if the glass is carefully turned sideways, sideways too), so pressure is not only downward
If a learner thinks pressure exists only in tyres or balloons, connect the gauge and demos to the open air around them right now
activities.intendedInsight: Invisible air is real matter with mass: pumping extra air into a ball makes it measurably heavier, and the whole atmosphere of air above us presses on us as air pressure that acts in all directions, not only downward.
learnerActions: Predict whether an inflated ball weighs more, less, or the same as the deflated ball and say why, then weigh both on a sensitive balance to check
Observe (or model) a crush-the-can demonstration and the upturned-glass-of-water-on-card demonstration, describing what the air is doing
Climb through the layers while watching a pressure gauge fall as altitude rises (and, within the troposphere, the temperature drop), and describe how air thins with height
Answer: if air presses on us all the time, why don't we feel squashed? And which direction(s) does air pressure push?
activities.title: Feel that air is real matter: weigh it and watch pressure

feedback: If a learner conflates the atmosphere with the ozone or greenhouse idea alone, clarify these are distinct roles of the air, not the whole thing
Reinforce correct Earth-system links by naming the specific spheres being connected (e.g. atmosphere and hydrosphere in the water cycle)
activities.intendedInsight: The atmosphere performs distinct roles — protection from radiation, warming, and carrying weather — and acts as one interacting Earth system rather than a single undifferentiated 'ozone/greenhouse' idea.
learnerActions: Match each described job to the air: shielding us from harmful radiation, keeping the planet warm enough for life, and holding our weather
Explain how the atmosphere links to the greenhouse effect and the water cycle so it is seen as an active system, not just 'the sky'
Describe one way the atmosphere interacts with another Earth sphere (geosphere, hydrosphere, or biosphere)
Distinguish the protective/warming roles of the air from its layered physical structure, noting they are different ideas
activities.title: Separate the atmosphere's roles and connect it to Earth systems

feedback: If answers drift from the structure, redirect to the cross-section and have the learner point to the relevant layer
Encourage linking altitude, thinning air, and the troposphere/weather location
activities.intendedInsight: Everyday aviation experience makes thinning air with altitude and the location of weather concrete and relatable.
learnerActions: Pose questions to a pilot or atmospheric scientist about how air thins with altitude and why it is clearer above most of the weather
Connect their answers back to the layered cross-section and the pressure gauge
Summarise which layer planes typically fly in and why the air is thinner there
activities.title: Ask a pilot or atmospheric scientist (optional extension)
